sections.what: Easter Seals Greater Houston provides disability services for children, adults, veterans and their families. Programs include early intervention, therapy, respite, assistive technology and family support. Our initial model combines a conditional child-health and caregiver-resource channel, not every program’s value.
sections.monitoring: Request current unique ECI households, completed therapy and incremental function against public and school alternatives, plus caregiver net resources. The 2023 annual report describes 7,662 ECI children and 81,078 hours; hours are not additional people. Current homepage lists over 14,500 disability and military neighbors, not all clinical successes. Audit page labels an annual report 2024, but the linked annual-report page exposes a 2023 PDF.
sections.qualitative: A plausible connection between completed therapy, function and caregiver resources. Local services and public-insurance alternatives are described in current primary sources. Latest audited whole-recipient costs include fundraising costs without adding donor benefits twice. Our child reference is historical, and household deduplication and causal response are judgments. Existing Medicaid, CHIP, insurers and school services reduce additional impact attributable to this provider. Whole annual cost versus a partial channel does not identify the next unrestricted gift’s return. Local operating EIN 74-1238418, not the national Easterseals affiliate. The official donation route supports Greater Houston services.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $22.21 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 12.083563 clinical QALYs and 1.401940 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.004502 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $29,957,609. Judged mapping: historical 7,662 ECI child opportunities × household uniqueness 0.9 × incremental access 0.25 gives 1,723.95 exposed households. Clinical response 0.3 gives 517.185 child health responders at utility 0.015 for two years after a half-year delay. All exposed households retain a full 0.0005 QALY harm and $100 access burden. A 20% caregiver resource response gets $1,500 one-year disposable work resources and $100 otherwise-paid household medical savings; positive components alone receive overlap 0.5. No child lifetime earnings are counted. Houston share 0.85 is a catchment hypothesis, not observed geography. Union 1723.95 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 517.185; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $30,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Caregiver work resources are after taxes, benefit withdrawals, commuting and childcare, not gross wages or time valued twice. Access fees and foregone access time remain in the full separate burden. Household medical savings must be actual otherwise-paid cash, not insured reimbursement or retail therapy value. Insurer, public-payer and substitute-provider opportunity costs remain unknown centrally and have adverse scenarios; recipient recognized spending is already in the numerator and must not be subtracted a second time as the same cost. External payer costs scale by Houston-attributed recipient exposures once, then a distinct dispersed payer pathway uses editionShare 1; no second local haircut removes those costs. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: Public contributions cover gaps alongside government grants, insurer reimbursements and fees. The homepage’s $100 therapy-hour appeal is not a verified marginal clinical outcome. No additional donor-funded completed cohort has been demonstrated. The FY 2025 audit has an unmodified opinion but identifies significant deficiencies involving recording support, conditional grants and opening balances; these are control findings, not a fraud finding.

model.costScope: Full audited FY 2025 operating recipient expenses, including direct donor benefits, versus a partial child-health and caregiver-resource channel.
model.geographicAttribution: ECI’s twelve-county catchment exceeds Houston MSA; judged local share 0.85.
model.formula: Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − N × unique × b × union harm discounted at onset) × edition share. Income = signed joint household log welfare equivalents with positive-only overlap and full costs. Better-life cost = 10 × full annual cost / (health + income), only when combined benefits are positive.
model.counterfactual: Medicaid, CHIP, private insurance, other therapists, school and early-intervention providers and family support retained.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Historical children served and service hours; current disability services, not observed causal QALYs or earnings.
